items.title: 672 to 676 Birchmount Road - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Approval
items.topics: development, official plan amendments, residential properties, rezoning; developing land; development (land); land development, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, residential real estate
items.brief: City staff recommend approving Official Plan and zoning changes to allow a seven-storey residential building with 226 homes at 672-676 Birchmount Road. The building would total about 18,300 square metres with two levels of underground parking. Council would amend the planning rules to permit the project.

items.title: 191-199 College Street and 74-76 Henry Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
items.topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
items.brief: City Council will decide whether to grow an approved College Street development from 31 to 45 storeys, raising the home count from 490 to 684, including 545 affordable rentals. The 2024 approval for the site's 408 affordable units carries a $27.7 million financial impact.

items.title: Pothole Blitz and Local Road Repair Strategy
items.topics: potholes, road repairs, transportation; crack repairs; cut repairs; fixing potholes; pothole repairs, pot holes; sink holes; sinkholes, transportation services
items.brief: Mayor Chow is asking Council to have Transportation Services run an ongoing pothole blitz strategy informed by road conditions and 311 data, building on the Fixing Roads Faster program. The 2026 budget put $11 million in new funding into expanding local road resurfacing, after crews filled over 250,000 potholes in 2025. It affects drivers on local roads across the city.

items.title: 2026 Operating and Capital Budget
items.brief: The Mayor's proposed 2026 operating and capital budgets, which the City of Toronto Act requires the Mayor to table for council's consideration, set out how the City plans to spend on services and capital projects in the coming year: an $18.86 billion operating budget and a $63.06 billion 10-year capital budget and plan (2026–2035). The proposal includes a 2.2 percent property tax increase, inclusive of the City Building Fund. The budget documents frame the proposal against a $1.8 billion shortfall in 2023, followed by a credit-rating upgrade to AA+, and project $250 million in revenue from the Vacant Homes Tax and luxury homes tax to fund affordability measures for working families. The budget touches every Toronto household — services, tax rates and projects across all wards. The source tables cite hundreds of additional line-item figures that are not summarized here.
